benchmark_info.name: CheeseBench: VLM Benchmark for Behavioral Neuroscience
benchmark_info.description: Evaluation of Vision-Language Models on classical behavioral neuroscience paradigms with published rodent baselines
benchmark_info.protocol: Unified - identical prompt for all tasks, no task-specific hints

environments.name: MorrisWaterMaze
environments.description: Circular water pool with hidden escape platform. Agent must use distal landmarks for spatial navigation.
environments.success_criterion: Navigate to hidden platform cell (reward > 0 on reaching platform position)

source.quote: C57BL/6 mice were tested in a Morris water maze over 8 acquisition sessions (5 trials/session). Path length decreased across sessions, with approximately 87% developing spatial search strategies.

original_paper.title: Spatial localization does not require the presence of local cues

environments.name: TMaze
environments.description: T-shaped maze for testing spatial working memory and alternation behavior.
environments.success_criterion: Enter rewarded arm on free-choice run (alternation from forced arm)

source.quote: In the forced alternation task, each trial consists of a forced choice run followed by a free choice run. A mouse is subjected to 10 consecutive trials in a session per day.

original_paper.title: Purpose and cognition: the determiners of animal learning

environments.name: BarnesMaze
environments.description: Circular platform with holes around perimeter. Agent must find escape hole using spatial cues.
environments.success_criterion: Navigate to escape hole among 20 options (reward > 0 on entering correct hole)

source.quote: B6C3F1/J mice were tested on a 12-hole Barnes maze over 5 sessions (4 trials/session). Primary errors decreased across sessions as mice learned to locate the escape hole.

original_paper.title: Memory deficits associated with senescence
original_paper.journal: Journal of Comparative and Physiological Psychology

environments.name: RadialArmMaze
environments.description: Central platform with 8 radiating arms. Tests working memory (don't revisit) and reference memory (only some arms rewarded).
environments.success_criterion: Collect all rewards from baited arms without revisiting depleted arms (0 working memory errors)

source.quote: Subjects are required to avoid arms previously used for escape during each testing day (working memory) as well as avoid fixed arms which never contain escape platforms (reference memory).

original_paper.title: Remembrance of places passed: Spatial memory in rats
original_paper.journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Animal Behavior Processes

animal_baseline.notes: 8 arms, 4 baited. WM errors: 3.5 -> 0.8 over 6 sessions

environments.name: OperantChamber
environments.description: Skinner box with lever and food magazine. Tests instrumental conditioning and learning.
environments.success_criterion: Press active lever to obtain food reward (reward > 0 on lever press)

source.quote: Animals were trained to press the lever to receive pellets from the feeder using a fixed-ratio (1:1) schedule. Sessions lasted for 20 min.

environments.name: ShuttleBox
environments.description: Two-chamber apparatus for active avoidance learning. Agent must escape to other side when warning signal appears.
environments.success_criterion: Shuttle to opposite chamber before shock onset (avoidance response within CS-US interval)

source.quote: Each trial consisted of 10 sec of conditioned stimulus, immediately followed by a scrambled electric shock. Crossing from one side to the other compartment terminated the CS or UCS presentation.

original_paper.title: Fear as an intervening variable in avoidance conditioning

environments.name: PlacePreference
environments.description: Two distinct chambers for conditioned place preference. Tests reward-context association learning.
environments.success_criterion: Spend >55% time in reward-paired chamber during post-conditioning test

source.quote: The procedure consists of three phases: Pre-Conditioning, Conditioning, and Post-Conditioning. Compartments have different floor textures and wall colors.

original_paper.title: Affective states associated with morphine injections

environments.name: StarMaze
environments.description: Five-arm water maze with central pentagonal hub. Tests allocentric vs egocentric navigation strategies through sequential spatial choices.
environments.cognitive_domain: Allocentric Spatial Navigation / Temporal Order Memory
environments.success_criterion: Navigate from start arm to goal arm via optimal spatial path (reward > 0 on reaching goal)

protocol_phases.day_0_pretraining: Visible platform in goal arm, no distal cues, teaches escape behavior
protocol_phases.day_1_to_10_training: Hidden platform in goal arm, distal cues present, 4 trials per session
protocol_phases.day_11_probe: Start from novel arm to test allocentric vs egocentric strategy

source.quote: The starmaze task relied on a massed training phase given over one day, composed of 10 sessions of 4 trials in the presence of all visual cues.

original_paper.title: Impaired sequential egocentric and allocentric memories in forebrain-specific-NMDA receptor knock-out mice during a new task dissociating strategies of navigation

key_references.title: Assessing Spatial Learning and Memory in Rodents
Complementary roles of the hippocampus and the dorsomedial striatum during spatial and sequence-based navigation behavior
A new approach for modeling episodic memory from rodents to humans: The temporal order memory

environments.name: DNMSTask
environments.description: Delayed non-match to sample task. Agent must remember sample stimulus and choose different one after delay.
environments.success_criterion: Select non-matching stimulus location after delay (2AFC: choose novel location)

source.quote: TUNL working memory task requires animals to non-match to a sample location after a delay. A correct response to the novel location leads to reward delivery.

original_paper.title: An analysis of short-term visual memory in the monkey
original_paper.journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Animal Behavior Processes
